content.title: About
content.content: Rotisserie chicken wings are tender pieces of meat roasted until the skin turns golden and crispy. The rotating spit keeps the meat juicy while the skin becomes crunchy. They are commonly served as a snack in fast‑food restaurants and at picnics.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings are cooked on a rotating spit, which ensures even heat distribution.
They are often marinated in a blend of spices, soy sauce, and honey for a sweet‑spicy flavor.
In the US the “Buffalo wings” style, coated in a hot sauce, is especially popular.
Chicken wings are one of the most popular bar foods during sports events.
Rotisserie cooking reduces the need for added fat compared to deep‑frying.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken wings provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain B6 and B12, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from chicken helps maintain healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Wings fit well into low‑carb diets such as keto.

items.title: Provides zinc
items.content: Zinc is important for immune health and wound healing.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Marinades and sauces often contain a lot of salt, which can be an issue for hypertension.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Skin‑on wings contain saturated fats; moderation is recommended.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper cooking can lead to salmonella; ensure internal temperature reaches 74 °C (165 °F).

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wings are typically served hot with dipping sauces (barbecue, hot, garlic). They are hand‑eaten by pulling the meat off the bone. They can be added to salads, rice bowls, or used in tacos.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh raw wings keep in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Cooked wings can be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 2 months.
